decisions.thought: Choice Scarf Gholdengo outspeeds Great Tusk (even Booster Energy Speed variants without sun) and targets its frail Special Defense. Make It Rain deals massive damage, with a very high chance to OHKO standard Great Tusk sets on turn 1 or heavily dent any switch-in.

Opponent's Gholdengo is at -1 SpA after Make It Rain. Ting-Lu is our premier special wall with Vessel of Ruin, completely blanking Gholdengo's attacks, threatening an OHKO with Earthquake, and giving us free momentum to set Stealth Rock.

Gholdengo is locked into Make It Rain at -1 SpA against Ting-Lu, which completely walls it and threatens an OHKO with Earthquake. Switching to Ogerpon-Wellspring applies immediate offensive pressure with STAB Water/Grass moves and forces Ting-Lu on the back foot.

Gholdengo is at -1 Special Attack after knocking out Great Tusk on Turn 1 with Make It Rain (likely Choice Specs/Scarf). Ting-Lu takes almost nothing from Gholdengo at -1 SpA thanks to Vessel of Ruin and massive bulk. STAB Earthquake threatens an immediate OHKO if Gholdengo stays in, while also dealing massive damage to grounded switch-ins.

Ogerpon-Wellspring threatens Ting-Lu with massive super-effective STAB damage (Ivy Cudgel / Horn Leech / Power Whip / Swords Dance). Staying in with Ting-Lu is extremely risky and invites either a KO or free setup.
Dragonite with Multiscale and Heavy-Duty Boots is a premier answer to Ogerpon-Wellspring. Dragonite quad-resists Grass and resists Water, taking negligible damage from Ivy Cudgel / Horn Leech even if Ogerpon clicks Swords Dance.
Switching Dragonite in directly completely walls Ogerpon-W's dual STABs and forces the opponent into a difficult prediction, allowing Dragonite to begin setting up Dragon Dance or forcing Ogerpon out.

Dragonite's Multiscale is broken at 87% HP. Ogerpon-Wellspring outspeeds Dragonite naturally. Play Rough targets Dragonite's Dragon/Flying typing for 4x super-effective damage, securing a clean OHKO from this HP range.

Dragonite easily walls Ogerpon-Wellspring's primary STABs (Ivy Cudgel is quad-resisted). Most Ogerpon-Wellspring sets run Ivy Cudgel, Horn Leech/Power Whip, Knock Off/U-turn, and Swords Dance/Spikes, lacking Play Rough.

Setting up with Dragon Dance forces immediate pressure, allowing Dragonite to threaten either a massive sweep or trade favorably with Extreme Speed next turn.

Ogerpon-Wellspring outspeeds Dragonite at +1 (max speed Jolly Ogerpon reaches 350, while Dragonite sits at 336). At 18.4% HP, Dragonite faints to any attack, including Ivy Cudgel or Play Rough.

Extreme Speed is essential for priority (+2). Unboosted Normal Extreme Speed deals ~57-67%, failing to KO from 77%. Tera Normal Extreme Speed boosts power to 76-90%, giving an almost guaranteed knockout after prior damage without taking a hit.

Dragonite is at +1 Attack and +1 Speed with 19% HP remaining.
At 229/301 HP (76.1%), Ogerpon-Wellspring easily survives a +1 Adamant Extreme Speed (max 67.1% / 202 HP).
Ivy Cudgel is 100% accurate and easily deals over 19% damage to finish Dragonite, avoiding Play Rough's 10% miss chance.

Dragonite is at 19% HP, Tera Normal, and boosted to +1 Atk and +1 Spe, likely looking to click Extreme Speed.
Gholdengo is Ghost-type, making it completely immune to Extreme Speed. Furthermore, Choice Scarf Gholdengo reaches 439 Speed, naturally outspeeding +1 Dragonite (max 394 Spe) even without priority. This makes Gholdengo a completely safe entry that guarantees the revenge kill next turn.

Dragonite at +1 Spe (336 Speed) outspeeds Gholdengo (max 293). Extreme Speed does zero damage due to Ghost typing. At +1 Atk, Earthquake cleanly OHKOs Gholdengo unless it holds an Air Balloon. Earthquake is the only correct offensive play.

Dragonite is Tera Normal at 19% HP and boosted (+1 Atk, +1 Spe).
Gholdengo is immune to Tera Normal Extreme Speed thanks to its Ghost typing.
With Choice Scarf (effective 439.5 Speed), Gholdengo outspeeds +1 Dragonite (max 426 Speed) and cleanly KOs it with Make It Rain (Dragonite is immune to Shadow Ball).

Dragonite fainted to Make It Rain, leaving opponent Gholdengo at -1 SpA. Choice Specs Dragapult is the premier offensive response here. It naturally outspeeds Gholdengo and threatens an immediate OHKO with Specs Shadow Ball, forcing either a defensive Tera or a switch, allowing me to seize game momentum.
Dragapult with Choice Specs naturally outspeeds Gholdengo (421 vs max 293) and easily OHKOs it with STAB Shadow Ball. Firing off Shadow Ball is the lowest-risk, highest-reward play.

Gholdengo is locked into Make It Rain at -1 SpA. While Choice Scarf outspeeds non-Scarf Dragapult, -1 Make It Rain cannot OHKO Dragapult from full HP, leaving Gholdengo vulnerable to a super-effective Ghost move. Kingambit resists Ghost and Dragon attacks, is immune to Shadow Ball, has Lum Berry for Will-O-Wisp, and threatens with Sucker Punch / Kowtow Cleave. Switching to Kingambit is the safest play.

Dragapult is locked into Shadow Ball via Choice Specs against a Kingambit that resists it and threatens an OHKO with Sucker Punch or Kowtow Cleave. Staying in is not an option.

Switching to Ting-Lu is the optimal, safe play. Ting-Lu sits at full health, effortlessly walls Kingambit's STAB attacks with its massive bulk and Vessel of Ruin, and threatens an immediate OHKO/2HKO with Earthquake.

Dragapult threatens Kingambit with potential coverage (Flamethrower/Hydro Pump/Will-O-Wisp), but Sucker Punch at +1 Supreme Overlord easily OHKOs standard Dragapult. Kingambit holds Lum Berry, safeguarding against Will-O-Wisp status cheese. Sucker Punch is the safest play to eliminate their fastest threat immediately.
Ting-Lu comfortably walls Kingambit and threatens an immediate knockout with STAB super-effective Earthquake at 69% HP. Earthquake is the safest and most optimal play here.

Ting-Lu threatens Kingambit with STAB Earthquake, which will KO from 68% HP. Kingambit must be preserved for the endgame. Switching to Iron Valiant creates immediate offensive pressure against Ting-Lu with STAB Fairy/Fighting coverage.

Ting-Lu cannot Terastallize as the opponent already burned Tera on Dragonite. Ting-Lu has Vessel of Ruin lowering special attack, making Close Combat hit significantly harder than Moonblast against typical specially defensive Ting-Lu spreads, comfortably putting it in range to be finished off.

Ting-Lu at 100% HP easily survives any single attack from Iron Valiant (even standard Choice Band or Life Orb Close Combat fails to OHKO standard Ting-Lu, while special Fairy moves do less than 50% due to Vessel of Ruin and Ting-Lu's SpD investment). In return, Earthquake deals over 60% to Iron Valiant, cleanly picking up the knockout on its remaining 57% HP without risking switches to Gholdengo or Dragapult.

Samurott-Hisui matches up excellently against Ting-Lu at 57% HP. Sharpness-boosted Razor Shell deals massive super-effective damage and threatens an immediate KO. Samurott is at full HP with Focus Sash intact, guaranteeing at least one safe action regardless of Ting-Lu's Earthquake.

Hisuian Samurott's Sharpness-boosted Razor Shell hits Ting-Lu super-effectively for massive damage, with a very high probability to KO from 57% HP. Samurott has Focus Sash intact, so there is no risk of being OHKOed.

Ting-Lu at 56.8% HP comfortably survives a single hit from Hisuian Samurott (Razor Shell, Ceaseless Edge, or Sacred Sword from 252 Atk Sharpness does at most ~50%). Switching out risks sacrificing or crippling Kingambit, Gholdengo, or Dragapult to Dark/Water/Fighting coverage. Staying in to hit Samurott-H with Earthquake is the best play to chunk it down into KO range while absorbing the incoming hit.

Dragapult outspeeds Hisuian Samurott naturally and threatens an immediate OHKO with Choice Specs Draco Meteor, or can pivot with U-turn on an expected switch to Kingambit or Gholdengo. Sending Kingambit or Gholdengo risks taking heavy Dark/Water/Fighting damage. Dragapult is the optimal bring.

Choice Specs Dragapult outspeeds Hisuian Samurott (421 vs max 295) and easily OHKOs it with Draco Meteor (117.1 - 138.3%), denying Ceaseless Edge spikes. It also deals heavy chip to anything trying to switch in. Draco Meteor is the decisive, high-value move.

Dragapult is weak to Dark and opponent has already used Tera. Samurott-Hisui is at 100% with Focus Sash intact, guaranteeing survival against any single hit. Knock Off has 100% accuracy and guarantees an OHKO on Dragapult.

Hamurott is at 1% HP with Knock Off. Gholdengo is 4x weak to Dark / Air Balloon popped and potentially outsped (base 84 vs base 85). Kingambit 4x resists Dark, easily tanks any hit from Hamurott, and has 4 Supreme Overlord boosts to clean the rest of the opponent's team.

Samurott-Hisui is at 1 HP and outspeeds Kingambit. The opponent will likely click Sucker Punch or an attacking move to clean up. If they don't use Sucker Punch (e.g. Swords Dance, Iron Head, Kowtow Cleave), Ceaseless Edge secures entry hazards on their side, putting immense pressure on Kingambit and their final Pokemon. Sacrificing Samurott for potential Spikes is optimal.

Opposing Hisuian Samurott is at 1% HP. Whether it goes for Ceaseless Edge, Razor Shell, or Sacred Sword, all of its standard productive plays involve attacking moves. 

Using Sucker Punch guarantees taking no damage and cleanly removes Samurott before it can set Spikes or deal heavy chip to Kingambit, preserving Kingambit at 100% HP with Supreme Overlord stacked to clean up the rest of the opponent's team.

Using Kowtow Cleave guarantees the KO regardless of Sucker Punch mindgames, as we survive their hit and KO in return, or KO directly if they do not attack.

Our Kingambit is at 23 HP and will faint to any hit. If opponent clicks Sucker Punch or Kowtow Cleave, we want to maximize damage output before going down. If they click Kowtow Cleave expecting a Sucker Punch mindgame, Kowtow Cleave punishes directly. Kingambit just fainted and we need to choose between Ribombee and Gholdengo.
Opponent's Kingambit has 4 Supreme Overlord boosts and has Sucker Punch / Kowtow Cleave, which completely threatens Choice Scarf Gholdengo (Steel/Ghost is weak to Dark). 
Ribombee has full HP and an intact Focus Sash (no entry hazards on field), guaranteeing it can survive any hit from Kingambit and retaliate or cripple it with Stun Spore / Moonblast.

Therefore, Ribombee is the safest and most optimal send-in.

Ribombee has a full HP Focus Sash, ensuring survival against any single attack from Kingambit.
Kingambit is Dark/Steel, so Fairy-type Moonblast deals neutral damage.
Clicking Moonblast chips Kingambit safely. If Kingambit uses Sucker Punch or Kowtow Cleave/Iron Head, Ribombee's Sash preserves it to attack again or allow Scarf Gholdengo to clean up.

Opponent has Ribombee and Gholdengo remaining, with Tera already used.
Kingambit has 4 Supreme Overlord boosts. Iron Head hits Ribombee super effectively for an easy OHKO (or breaks Focus Sash if present). Sucker Punch is risky because Ribombee frequently clicks Sticky Web or Stun Spore. Iron Head is the safest and most lethal option.

Ribombee is at 1% HP and outspeeds Kingambit. Moonblast from Ribombee threatens to KO Kingambit from 27.2% HP. Priority Sucker Punch secures the KO before Ribombee can attack, preserving Kingambit to deal with Gholdengo.

Ribombee is at 1 HP against a 28% HP Kingambit. Kingambit has Sucker Punch.
Clicking Moonblast forces Kingambit to use Sucker Punch (or die immediately if it predicts a switch and clicks Kowtow Cleave/Iron Head).
When Ribombee goes down to Sucker Punch, Choice Scarf Gholdengo enters at 100% HP completely undamaged to cleanly revenge KO and win the game. Switching directly risks Gholdengo taking a massive boosted Kowtow Cleave.

Kingambit is at 34% HP and has Sucker Punch. Make It Rain is our strongest attack to secure the KO. Make It Rain deals guaranteed fatal damage to Kingambit from 34% HP.
